questions.reason: Measuring height in edges, the minimum N(1) is 2. For h ≥ 2, a child of height h − 1 needs N(h − 1) nodes, and its sibling needs at least N(h − 1) − 2. That smaller size is attainable by a perfect tree or the empty tree, so N(h) = 2N(h − 1) − 1 = 2^(h − 1) + 1.
questions.note: The printed labels (2) and (4) correspond to app options B and D. Explicitly define height as the number of edges on a longest root-to-leaf path.
